label: WardStock - Status Heartbeat
info:
Runs every 15 minutes (PLAN.md §15). Deliberately a fifth, dedicated flow rather than each sync flow pushing its own status inline — reads the shared job_status SQLite table every status-writing flow now maintains (Aug 2026 SQLite migration, see below), computes one consolidated snapshot, pushes it to GoDaddy's api/status_push.php (feeds status.php's HA/Node-RED/Analytics view), and writes the same snapshot to InfluxDB's system_status_snapshot measurement per Ward's explicit request to keep it there for trend-watching.

SQLite MIGRATION (Aug 2026) — this flow used to chain 28 api-current-state HA reads (4 fields × 7 flows), one per helper entity, each needing its own manually-configured Server field. Replaced with a single SELECT * FROM job_status against /share/lucius_status.db (the same file every flow's job_success/job_failed nodes write to) — no HA connection needed for this flow at all anymore. dashboard.yaml's old Lovelace card, which showed 3 of these flows' HA entities directly, is retired along with the entities themselves — status.php and this flow's own InfluxDB write are now the only places this data lives.

UNTESTED, same caveat as every flow in this project — PLUS one piece of real, deliberate scope-narrowing worth knowing about: PLAN.md §15 suggested this flow also query HA's own /api/config for HA version/uptime, to give the 'HA' category more than just a heartbeat. That's NOT implemented here — it would need either a Supervisor API token or a manually-managed long-lived access token, neither of which this project otherwise needs. Instead, the 'ha' category's only component (ha_core) uses this heartbeat's own successful execution as the signal — which is still real signal: if HA/Node-RED goes down, this flow stops running, ha_core goes overdue on status.php, and that overdue state IS the answer to 'is HA up.' Richer HA-native detail is a clearly flagged open follow-up, not a silent gap.
